title: Correct orbital period
description: Essential: The response must correctly state or use the geostationary satellite's orbital period of 86400 s (24 hours).

title: Correct final time
description: Essential: The final numerical answer for the minimum wait time must be approximately 0.48 s.

title: Applies Newton's law
description: Important: The solution must apply Newton's law of gravitation and set it equal to the centripetal force for the satellite.

title: Calculates orbital height
description: Important: The solution must correctly solve for the satellite's height h above Earth's surface, obtaining approximately 3.59e7 m.

title: Identifies signal path
description: Important: The solution must recognize that the shortest communication path involves a round trip distance of 2h (or 2√(R+h)² - R²) for the electromagnetic signal.

title: Uses speed of light
description: Important: The solution must correctly use the speed of light c to compute the signal travel time.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: All quantities are used with consistent SI units throughout the calculation.

title: Confuses orbital radius
description: Pitfall: Using Earth's radius R instead of the orbital radius (R+h) in the force or distance equations.

title: One-way time error
description: Pitfall: Calculating only the one-way travel time instead of the round-trip time for a response.
